coverage: Two distinct administrator identities create update and enable reviews while the managed app is in the states required by each plan.

The native update and enable confirmations run concurrently against the real runtime observation and production review-consume paths. Update is refused as stale/conflicting; enable creates the only pending lifecycle operation.

The same pattern runs against repair: update and the normal browser repair confirmation execute concurrently. The browser repair plan is the sole consumed plan and operation; update remains unconsumed.
Both races assert exactly one pending update/enable or update/repair operation and exactly one consumed review. No live tuple or authority is changed by the losing contender.
The native matrix then executes the winning enable/repair through the real runner and completes the remaining lifecycle through uninstall, data removal and fresh reinstall.
limits: This is disposable development acceptance with two server-side administrator sessions and the real signed runner path, not a production load or SLO claim.
The browser repair confirmation is the second operator in the repair race; the update contender is a real Portal management review from a separate administrator session.
Production deployment, external monitoring and the remaining H16-H18 release gates remain separate.
